justifications.functional_suitability: Covers all functional requirements with dedicated containers: Patient Registration for R-01, Appointment Scheduling for R-02, EMR Service with Encryption and Audit Service for R-03, and Billing & Insurance Service for R-04. However, resource clash check mechanisms in Appointment Service are only superficially described.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Asynchronous messaging (Event Publisher, retry queues) and read replicas in Billing Database Repository are provided, but no caching or query optimization mechanisms are specified for EMR Service to guarantee the <1 s P95 screen load target.
justifications.compatibility: Explicitly addresses R-08 via FHIR Integration Client and HL7 FHIR Integration Engine, providing compliant interoperability with External Lab & Imaging Systems and Insurance/Third-Party Payer Gateway using standardized FHIR protocols.
justifications.usability: All identified stakeholders (Patient, Clinician/Doctor, Receptionist, Billing Specialist, Administrator) access services through a unified Web/Mobile Frontend and API Gateway, although distinct front-end views or workflows per role are not detailed.
justifications.reliability: Includes WORM Archive Storage for 10-year retention and asynchronous retry queues. However, concrete mechanisms for active-active multi-region failover and data synchronization between on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1 needed for 99.99% availability are missing.
justifications.security: Comprehensive security controls: Token Exchange Service enforces MFA and ABAC, Encryption and Audit Service provides field-level AES-256 and sidecar auditing, Database Cluster enforces AES-256, and Break-Glass Access Controller handles emergency access for HIPAA/GDPR.
justifications.maintainability: Excellent modularity across distinct microservice containers (Patient Registration, Appointment Scheduling, EMR Service, Billing & Insurance Service), each cleanly partitioned into controllers, business services, and repositories communicating via Istio mTLS.
justifications.portability: Standardized on containerized Spring Boot workloads on Kubernetes Ingress/Istio and S3-compatible APIs, allowing execution on both on-prem-k8s and cloud (eu-central-1), though hybrid deployment configurations are not detailed.

PERF-01.justification: EMR Service relies on synchronous REST and AES-256 field decryption without an explicit caching layer. Under 500 concurrent clinician requests, database load and cryptographic overhead risk exceeding the 1-second P95 latency threshold.
sensitivity_points: Cryptographic decryption latency under peak concurrent read traffic
Absence of an in-memory caching tier for active EMR records
tradeoffs: Field-level encryption ensures regulatory compliance but increases CPU overhead and read latency

PERF-02.justification: While asynchronous retry queues are noted at container level, the EMR component model lacks dedicated worker pools and buffer queues to decouple bulk FHIR ingestion from clinical read workloads, risking read degradation.
sensitivity_points: Resource contention between high-volume FHIR ingestion and synchronous clinical reads
tradeoffs: Co-locating FHIR ingestion in EMR service simplifies architecture but risks thread-pool exhaustion

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture lacks deployment definitions detailing cross-site active-active database replication, data synchronization, or GSLB failover across on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1. Achieving zero data loss and 1-minute recovery is unsubstantiated.
sensitivity_points: Cross-region database replication latency and consistency guarantees
Automated traffic failover routing between on-premises and cloud sites
tradeoffs: Active-active cross-site replication provides high availability but introduces complex network synchronization challenges

AVAIL-02.justification: Claims Service uses asynchronous retries to prevent claim loss during failures. However, sub-30-second database failover and explicit idempotent deduplication mechanisms are not described in the database or service architecture.
sensitivity_points: Database cluster failover detection time and connection pool recovery
Implementation of idempotency keys to prevent duplicate claim submissions
tradeoffs: Asynchronous claim retries ensure eventual consistency but require strict idempotency controls

MOD-01.justification: The architecture cleanly decouples Billing & Insurance from the EMR Service. Adding a new clearinghouse is isolated to the Claims Service component and external payer interface, leaving the rest of the system unchanged.
sensitivity_points: Isolation of clearinghouse-specific payload adapters within Claims Service
tradeoffs: Dedicated billing service limits blast radius of changes but introduces network overhead

MOD-02.justification: Adding an audited demographic field is bounded to Web/Mobile Frontend, Patient Registration (Admission Controller), and the Database Cluster schema. Separation from the EMR service keeps changes within three components.
sensitivity_points: Coupling between frontend form schema, admission validation, and persistence entities
tradeoffs: Separating registration from EMR bounds change scope but requires demographic synchronization downstream

SEC-01.justification: MFA is strictly enforced across perimeter relationships and Token Exchange Service before tokens are granted, preventing password-only breaches. However, automated security alerting within 1 minute lacks dedicated SIEM components.
sensitivity_points: Strict enforcement of multi-factor authentication prior to issuing session tokens
tradeoffs: Enforcing MFA at the gateway enhances perimeter security but introduces user friction

SEC-02.justification: ABAC policy enforcement and Break-Glass Access Controller govern unauthorized record access. The Encryption and Audit Service logs reads to WORM Archive Storage with Object Lock, ensuring tamper-evident retention for 10 years.
sensitivity_points: Direct streaming of sidecar audit logs to immutable WORM archive storage
tradeoffs: Auditing 100% of read access ensures compliance but generates massive long-term storage volumes
